I1.description: wide control: product + 6 month-name columns, numeric data rows

I2.description: long control: Product | Kuukausi | Myynti with one row per product-month

I3.description: unknown control: quarterly summary (Q1-Q4 + Vuosi), no month-name tokens

I4.description: transposed monthly table: months DOWN rows (Kuukausi column), products ACROSS columns; a transposed wide representation, not canonical long
I4.role: out-of-contract probe: the saved macro is knowingly WRONG here (det says long; expected unknown). Tests whether GLM notices the structural difference. First probe where the macro is allowed to be wrong.
I4.grader_note: For I4 the frozen fixture expectation is the grader: i_pass = (llm_label == unknown). The verifier's support check is SUSPENDED for I4 -- dl=12 is recorded as evidence but is NOT interpreted as support for 'long'. I4 exists to demonstrate that 'month tokens down one column' is not sufficient evidence for long format. The deterministic classifier is left UNCHANGED and knowingly wrong (det=long); do not 'fix' it before the run.

I5.description: CONTRASTIVE probe: SAME frozen I4 fixture (transposed monthly), but the LLM contract first shows two category prototypes (one WIDE, one LONG) then the target, and says 'Use unknown if it matches neither supplied representation.' Isolates whether the I4 failure was contract-underspecification or a contextual-classification limit.
I5.role: contrastive probe: same fixture/labels/expected as I4, ONLY change is the contract (word definitions -> two canonical prototypes). det_classify stays long (macro unchanged, wrong).
I5.grader_note: Same oracle grader as I4: i_pass = (llm_label == unknown); verifier suspended; dl=12 evidence not long-support. The prototypes are the ONLY change from I4. Do NOT name 'transposed wide' or give a rule like 'long requires one row per product-month' -- let the examples establish the distinction.

I6.description: MATCHED-LANGUAGE contrastive probe: same frozen I4 fixture, same labels/expected as I5, ONLY change from I5 is the prototype LANGUAGE (English -> Finnish), matching the target's language. Removes the cross-language confound that was I5's last stated caveat.
I6.role: matched-language I5: isolates cross-language role transfer. Finnish prototypes: WIDE = Tuote|Tammi|Helmi|Maalis; LONG = Tuote|Kuukausi|Myynti. det_classify stays long (macro unchanged, wrong).
I6.grader_note: Same oracle grader as I4/I5: i_pass = (llm_label == unknown); verifier suspended. Finnish prototypes are the ONLY change from I5. If I6 -> unknown: earlier failure was cross-language role transfer (examples should be linguistically aligned with source). If I6 -> wide/long: GLM wide/long not reliable for transposed monthly -- boundary located; stop tightening.

pass_criteria.i_pass_oracle_probes: llm_label == expected_format (unknown); verifier support SUSPENDED; dl=12 is evidence, not long-support  (I4/I5/I6)
pass_criteria.i1_i2_i3_pass: I1 AND I2 AND I3 all i_pass (frozen 3-probe classifier result, committed f3c3a9a)
pass_criteria.i4_pass: I4.i_pass (LLM says unknown on word-definition contract)
pass_criteria.i5_pass: I5.i_pass (LLM says unknown on English-prototype contract)
pass_criteria.i6_pass: I6.i_pass (LLM says unknown on Finnish-prototype contract)

counterfactual: det_classify == expected_format per probe (non-scoring for pass, recorded). For I4/I5/I6 det_classify=long != expected=unknown -> recorded counterfactual MISS (the saved macro is wrong on this representation; unchanged across I4/I5/I6).

decision_table.probes: I1 & I2 pass, I3 not run

decision_table.outcome: I4 PASS -- macro wrong, GLM caught it (word contract)
I4 FAIL -- GLM did not catch it (word contract)
I5 PASS -- prototypes fixed it: contract UNDERSPECIFIED
I5 FAIL -- prototypes did not fix it (English prototypes)
I6 PASS -- Finnish prototypes fixed it: earlier failure was CROSS-LANGUAGE role transfer (align examples with source language)
I6 FAIL -- even matched-language prototypes do not fix it: boundary LOCATED (GLM wide/long not reliable for transposed monthly). STOP tightening.

stated_limitations: The deterministic classifier is a coarse month-token heuristic. It is correct on the clean wide/long controls and the no-month (quarterly) case. It is KNOWINGLY WRONG on I4/I5/I6 (transposed wide): months land in a data column and the rule says 'long', but the expected label is 'unknown'. The classifier is left unchanged.

The gate is a VERIFIER, not an authority: it checks the LLM's label is objectively supported by the token criteria; it does not substitute its own answer (the criteria are too coarse to be authoritative, unlike H's coverage==12).

For I4/I5/I6 the verifier is SUSPENDED as the grader: dl=12 would make gate.supported(long)=true and gate.supported(unknown)=false, but that evidence rule is exactly what I4 falsified. The frozen fixture expectation (oracle) grades these probes. The verifier's support values are still recorded as evidence.

I5 prototypes are English; I6 prototypes are Finnish (matched to the target). I6 removes the cross-language confound that was I5's caveat. If I6 still fails, the cross-language explanation is ruled out and the boundary is located.
n=1 on GLM-5.2, no seed control: existence, not reliability.
Classification only. No unpivot/reshape/transformation is produced or evaluated (hard stop honored). No 'transposed_wide' fourth label is added.
